item.title: Introduction to Apache Kyuubi
item.description:
Apache Kyuubi is a multi-tenant SQL gateway for distributed data systems. It gives people and BI tools a stable JDBC or ODBC endpoint without requiring every user to manage Spark application lifecycles, cluster queues, or engine configuration.

Kyuubi separates a long-lived client endpoint from the processes that execute queries. This distinction is its main architectural contribution:

  • Kyuubi servers authenticate clients, maintain protocol sessions, select engines, and forward operations.
  • Kyuubi engines run SQL and consume compute resources. Spark SQL is the most common engine, while Kyuubi releases can also integrate with other query engines.
  • External services still provide resource management, metadata, storage, authorization policy, and service discovery.

Kyuubi therefore does not replace Spark, YARN, Kubernetes, a Hive metastore, or object storage. It coordinates access to them.

item.title: Apache Hive / Kyuubi Overview
item.description:
Apache Hive provides SQL semantics over datasets stored in distributed filesystems and object stores. A Hive deployment is not one daemon or one storage format. It combines a SQL language, metadata services, query compilation, an execution engine, warehouse storage, and client protocols.

Several names surrounding Hive refer to different layers:

  1. Hive is the project, HiveQL language, compiler, optimizer, runtime integration, and supporting services.
  2. Hive Metastore (HMS) stores and serves table, partition, schema, location, statistics, and transaction metadata. HMS stores metadata rather than table data.
  3. HiveServer2 (HS2) accepts remote JDBC and ODBC sessions, compiles HiveQL, coordinates execution, and returns results.
  4. hive CLI is the historical thick command-line client. It loads Hive runtime code locally and should not be confused with HiveServer2.
  5. Beeline is a JDBC command-line client. Shared deployments use Beeline against HiveServer2 because authentication, configuration, auditing, and resource control remain on the server.
  6. Apache Kyuubi is a multi-tenant SQL gateway with a HiveServer2-compatible protocol. It can manage engines such as Spark SQL, but Kyuubi is not HiveServer2 and does not turn Spark SQL into the Hive execution engine.
  7. Kerberos authenticates users and services across Hadoop components. Kerberos does not define table schemas, execute SQL, or decide SQL privileges.
  8. Apache Kite SDK belongs to the historical Hadoop dataset-tooling ecosystem. It is not part of a current Hive query path.

The distinctions matter because a JDBC connection can succeed while HMS is unavailable, an HMS lookup can succeed while HDFS permissions reject a query, and a Kyuubi endpoint can speak the HiveServer2 protocol without executing Hive’s compiler or runtime.

item.title: MySQL Transactions, Isolation, and Concurrency
item.description:
InnoDB transactions protect database invariants by committing related changes atomically and controlling how concurrent statements observe them. Isolation is not a replacement for constraints: use primary, unique, foreign-key, and check constraints for invariants the schema can express, then select a transaction and locking pattern for multi-statement decisions.

item.title: MySQL SELECT Patterns
item.description:
SELECT can read rows, combine sources, filter, aggregate, order, and limit a result. A useful outline of its syntax is:

sql 
SELECT [DISTINCT] select_expr [, ...]
FROM table_references [PARTITION (partition_names)]
WHERE condition
GROUP BY group_expr [, ...]
HAVING condition
WINDOW window_name AS (window_spec) [, ...]
ORDER BY order_expr [ASC | DESC] [, ...]
LIMIT {row_count | offset, row_count | row_count OFFSET offset};

Logical query processing provides a model for reasoning about a result:

  1. FROM, including joins, constructs candidate rows.
  2. WHERE filters individual rows.
  3. GROUP BY forms groups and aggregate functions compute group values.
  4. HAVING filters groups; named windows are then available for window functions.
  5. The select list produces output columns, DISTINCT removes duplicate output rows, ORDER BY orders them, and LIMIT restricts the returned rows.

The optimizer is free to transform and reorder physical operations when the result preserves these semantics. For example, it can push a predicate into an index access or choose a different join order. Logical processing is therefore not an execution plan; use EXPLAIN or EXPLAIN ANALYZE to inspect the plan.

item.title: MyBatis Mapping
item.description:
MyBatis maps Java calls to SQL statements while JDBC owns parameter binding, statement execution, and result-set access. A mapper should make that boundary visible: SQL column names belong in the statement, Java property names belong in parameter and result mappings, and a type handler performs any nonstandard conversion between them.

item.title: Relational Data Modeling
item.description:
An entity-relationship model identifies entity types, their attributes, and relationships before choosing tables. A relational schema then represents each fact once at a defined grain. For example, order_line represents one product on one order, whereas order represents the order header.

Entities, Keys, and Relationships #

Every table needs a candidate key that uniquely identifies its rows. Choose a primary key that is stable, non-null, and suitable for joins. A surrogate key does not remove the need for unique constraints over natural business identities, such as an account’s external identifier.

item.title: MySQL String Types and Character Sets
item.description:
MySQL string columns have both a logical character limit and a physical byte representation. Keeping those ideas separate prevents many surprises with multilingual text and indexes.

CHAR and VARCHAR #

CHAR(n) is a fixed-length character string. MySQL pads values to its declared length for storage semantics, so it is best for genuinely fixed-width values such as country codes. VARCHAR(n) is variable length and is usually the better default for names, labels, and other text whose length varies.

item.title: MySQL Indexes
item.description:
InnoDB implements primary and secondary indexes with B+ trees. An index reduces I/O when its order matches selective predicates, joins, range scans, or ordering requirements; it increases write work and storage for every indexed row.

Clustered and Secondary Indexes #

An InnoDB table stores row data in its clustered index. InnoDB selects the declared primary key; otherwise it selects the first suitable non-null unique key, or creates an internal hidden key. Declare a short, stable primary key because each secondary-index entry stores the primary-key value.

item.title: MySQL Tables and Views
item.description:
A base table persists rows. A view persists a query definition and presents its result as a table-like object. SHOW FULL TABLES distinguishes them, and INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES.TABLE_TYPE reports BASE TABLE or VIEW.

InnoDB Row Formats #

InnoDB supports REDUNDANT, COMPACT, DYNAMIC, and COMPRESSED row formats. DYNAMIC is the current default. For variable-length columns, InnoDB can store long values on overflow pages and retain a reference in the clustered record. The precise inline and overflow behavior depends on the row format, page size, column type, and value length; schema design should avoid assuming that a TEXT or BLOB value occupies a fixed in-row size.

item.title: MySQL Variables and Prepared Statements
item.description:
MySQL distinguishes server system variables, local routine variables, and session user variables. Their scope and evaluation rules differ, so they should not be used interchangeably.

System and User Variables #

System variables use @@ and may have global, session, or both scopes:

sql 
SELECT @@GLOBAL.transaction_isolation, @@SESSION.sql_mode;
SET SESSION sql_safe_updates = 1;

Changing a global variable affects new sessions when the variable also has a session scope; it is not a way to change an existing connection’s transaction policy. A dynamic variable can change at runtime, whereas a read-only variable requires startup configuration. SET PERSIST changes the runtime global value and writes mysqld-auto.cnf; SET PERSIST_ONLY writes the persisted value without changing runtime state. Verify that a variable is persistable before using either form, and keep file ownership with the server rather than editing that generated file.

item.title: MySQL Server and Data Types
item.description:
MySQL separates server initialization, schema definition, and connection configuration. A production installation should initialize an empty data directory once, store configuration outside that directory, and manage the server through the platform service manager. mysqld --initialize creates the data dictionary and an initial administrative account; it does not configure an application schema or privileges.
